title: Pork Tonkatsu
subtitle: Japanese breaded pork cutlet with tonkatsu sauce
excerpt: The Japanese fried pork classic: a thick pork loin cutlet, pounded, coated in panko breadcrumbs, and deep-fried until the exterior is shattering-crisp and golden and the pork inside is just cooked and juicy. Served with shredded cabbage and the sweet-sharp tonkatsu sauce.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tonkatsu (ton = pork, katsu from the English 'cutlet') is a Japanese dish created in Tokyo in 1899 by the Western-style restaurant Rengatei, which adapted the European Wiener schnitzel using Japanese panko breadcrumbs. The panko coating, which is coarser and drier than European fine breadcrumbs, produces a dramatically crispier, lighter crust and became the defining element of the dish. Tonkatsu is now a staple of Japanese home cooking and restaurant menus, served with finely shredded raw cabbage (which provides freshness and texture contrast) and tonkatsu sauce (a thick, fruity brown sauce similar to Worcestershire). The sauce is available bottled (Bull-Dog is the most widely available brand) and is worth seeking out for authenticity.

content.text: Use pork loin steaks about 2 cm thick; chops with a bone can be used but the bone makes even frying more difficult. Pound them to an even thickness with a rolling pin or meat mallet. The oil temperature is critical: 170°C produces a golden-brown crust in the time it takes for the pork to cook through; too hot and it burns, too cool and it becomes greasy.

items.preparation: pork loin steaks about 2 cm thick; pounded to an even thickness

content.text: Make the tonkatsu sauce by mixing the Worcestershire sauce, ketchup, and soy sauce. Set aside. Season the pork. Set up a coating station: flour, beaten egg, and panko. Coat each pork steak in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing firmly to adhere.
Heat the oil to 170°C in a deep pan. Fry the tonkatsu one at a time for 4 to 5 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and the pork is cooked through. Drain on kitchen paper.
Slice the tonkatsu on the diagonal into thick pieces and arrange over a pile of shredded cabbage. Pour the tonkatsu sauce over. Serve with steamed white rice and pickled ginger.
